Irrationality of the dilogarithm at reciprocals of integers

Ruiyi Zhang Independent Researcher, Columbia, Maryland, USA
Abstract.

We prove that Li2⁡(1/n)\operatorname{Li}_{2}(1/n) is irrational for every nonzero integer nn. The proof combines a determinant criterion with exact fixed-base integerization, logarithmic-potential estimates, Frobenius nonvanishing, and a three-form Hermite–Padé construction. The finite positive range is treated by a common variational problem and two endpoint certificates; the negative middle range is handled by signed contour integrals at the six bases −2,…,−7-2,\ldots,-7; the two remaining tails follow from an explicit Hermite–Padé estimate. Every numerical constant used in the argument is given as a rational bound or an explicitly directed interval.

Key words and phrases:
dilogarithm, determinant, logarithmic energy, Hermite–Padé, Frobenius
2020 Mathematics Subject Classification:
Primary 11J72; Secondary 33B30

1. Introduction

For an integer ss with |s|≥2|s|\geq 2, irrationality of Li2⁡(1/s)\operatorname{Li}_{2}(1/s) was proved by Hata [5] for all s≤−5s\leq-5 and s≥7s\geq 7, and by Rhin and Viola [11] for s=6s=6. A recent preprint of Prellberg [10] treats s=−4,−3s=-4,-3 and 55. These works are cited for history only: no irrationality statement from them is used below, and the proof is self-contained. The cases s=−2,2,3,4s=-2,2,3,4 were open; among them is Li2⁡(1/2)=π2/12−(log⁡2)2/2\operatorname{Li}_{2}(1/2)=\pi^{2}/12-(\log 2)^{2}/2. For s=±1s=\pm 1 the values are rational multiples of π2\pi^{2}, which is irrational [8].

The general tools are the prime number theorem [2]; Kummer’s carry theorem [7] and Lucas’ congruence [9]; the Cauchy–Binet formula [4] and its integral form due to Andréief [1, 3]; Cauchy’s double-alternant determinant  [6]; logarithmic potential theory [12]; and Stirling’s formula [13].

We call the positive determinant P0 and the signed contour determinant V. These names refer to the two explicit constructions below.

The endpoint energy lower bounds and fixed-base field bounds are computer-assisted: directed interval arithmetic verifies them from the printed tables, with the algorithm and code supplied in the ancillary files.

The proof applies the criterion below to one defined determinant at a time. Sections 5–6 treat positive bases; Sections 9–10 treat the negative bases; Section 12 treats both tails, and Section 11 supplies eventual nonvanishing sequences. The final assembly checks the ranges and their boundary points.

2. Main theorem

For |z|≤1|z|\leq 1, put

Li2⁡(z)=∑r≥1zrr2.\operatorname{Li}_{2}(z)=\sum_{r\geq 1}\frac{z^{r}}{r^{2}}.
Theorem 2.1.

For every nonzero integer nn, the number Li2⁡(1/n)\operatorname{Li}_{2}(1/n) is irrational.

For n=1n=1 and n=−1n=-1 this follows from Li2⁡(1)=π2/6\operatorname{Li}_{2}(1)=\pi^{2}/6 and Li2⁡(−1)=−π2/12\operatorname{Li}_{2}(-1)=-\pi^{2}/12, together with the irrationality of π2\pi^{2} [8]; the determinant argument covers all |n|≥2|n|\geq 2.

2.1. Coverage map

The ranges below are disjoint and cover all remaining nonzero integers.

base range construction ingredients
±1\pm 1 classical evaluations π2\pi^{2}
2≤a≤112\leq a\leq 11 positive determinant arithmetic, energy, nonvanishing
−7≤a≤−2-7\leq a\leq-2 signed determinant arithmetic, contour energy, nonvanishing
a≥12a\geq 12 or a≤−8a\leq-8 three-form Hermite–Padé residues, integerization, saddle estimates

In each application of the criterion, the determinant, integerizer, analytic estimate, and nonvanishing sequence belong to the same polynomial family at the indicated base.

Gmk,a⁢(ξ)≠0(k≥k0).G_{m_{k},a}(\xi)\neq 0\qquad(k\geq k_{0}).

If α⁢(a)>τ⁢(a)\alpha(a)>\tau(a), then tt is irrational.

Indeed, if t=ξ=u/v∈ℚt=\xi=u/v\in\mathbb{Q} in lowest terms, then for every sufficiently large kk, vmk⁢Dmk,a⁢Gmk,a⁢(ξ)v^{m_{k}}D_{m_{k},a}G_{m_{k},a}(\xi) is a nonzero integer, while (3.1) and (3.2) make its absolute value tend to zero. The determinant, integerizer and nonvanishing statements must refer to the same polynomial.

5. Arithmetic for the positive determinant

This section proves the fixed-base denominator estimate for the P0 pencil. The base is fixed before the limit in mm is taken. No estimate uniform in unbounded |a||a| at finite mm is asserted. The proof has an algebraic part, an exact sum over primes, and a prime-number-theorem limit. The algebraic and limiting arguments below are all-mm arguments. The large-ratio contribution is specified by the rational table 5.1 and its type-generation rule.

For an indeterminate aa,

Δm⁢Gm⁢(T;a)∈ℤ⁢[a,T].\Delta_{m}G_{m}(T;a)\in\mathbb{Z}[a,T].

Lemma 10.1 (signed-energy concavity for fixed qq).

Let μ,ν\mu,\nu be triples of positive measures of masses (1,5/4,1)(1,5/4,1), supported in compact subsets of the indicated supports or their sufficiently small tubular neighborhoods. where the hatted fields are formed from ν\nu. Consequently the same inequality for the full energy is obtained by adding the displayed one-body terms to the hatted fields, i.e. by using Fx,Fv,FzF_{x},F_{v},F_{z} in the field bounds.

Proof.

By the shared quadratic-duality identity in Section C, it suffices to prove that the zero-mass quadratic remainder 𝒬q⁢(μ−ν)\mathcal{Q}_{q}(\mu-\nu) is nonpositive. The right side equals

The shared identity gives the asserted quadratic inequality. For a competitor μv\mu_{v} whose support meets zero, fix a smooth probability measure ρ\rho supported in [3/4,7/8][3/4,7/8]. For 0<δ<1/40<\delta<1/4, let λδ=μv|{|v|<δ}\lambda_{\delta}=\mu_{v}|_{\{|v|<\delta\}}, let eδ=λδ⁢(ℂ)e_{\delta}=\lambda_{\delta}(\mathbb{C}), and set

μv,δ=μv−λδ+eδ⁢ρ.\mu_{v,\delta}=\mu_{v}-\lambda_{\delta}+e_{\delta}\rho.

Finite logarithmic self-energy excludes an atom at zero, so eδ→0e_{\delta}\to 0 and μv,δ⇒μv\mu_{v,\delta}\Rightarrow\mu_{v}. Absolute integrability of the logarithmic pairings in 𝒬q\mathcal{Q}_{q} implies that the integrals over the deleted sets tend to zero. The replacement terms involving eδ⁢ρe_{\delta}\rho tend to zero as well: ρ\rho is separated from {|v|<δ}\{|v|<\delta\}, and its logarithmic potential is bounded on the compact supports. The kernel log⁡|q+u⁢v|\log|q+uv| is bounded and continuous on the stated tubes because q≥2q\geq 2 and |u|,|v|≤1+o⁢(1)|u|,|v|\leq 1+o(1). Hence 𝒬q⁢(μx,μv,δ,μz)→𝒬q⁢(μ)\mathcal{Q}_{q}(\mu_{x},\mu_{v,\delta},\mu_{z})\to\mathcal{Q}_{q}(\mu). The reference fields F^i\widehat{F}_{i} are continuous and bounded on these compact sets, so their integrals also converge. Applying the already proved inequality to μv,δ\mu_{v,\delta} and taking the limit proves the quadratic inequality without requiring ∫|log⁡|v||⁢𝑑μv<∞\int|\log|v||\,d\mu_{v}<\infty.

The one-body integrals in ℰq\mathcal{E}_{q} are then interpreted as extended real integrals. On the compact xx- and vv-supports, log⁡|w|\log|w| is bounded above and can have integral −∞-\infty; on the zz-support, |z|≥r−o⁢(1)|z|\geq r-o(1), so the zz-term is finite. Adding these linear terms to the quadratic inequality is therefore valid in the extended reals. In particular, when the full energy is −∞-\infty the asserted upper bound is automatic. This argument uses no implication from finite self-energy to a finite absolute logarithmic moment. ∎

11. Seed determinants and eventual nonvanishing

This section proves the nonvanishing input for the determinants used in each of the two constructions. The P0 family has a base-dependent auxiliary prime; the signed construction uses one explicitly listed prime for each base a=−ra=-r, 2≤r≤72\leq r\leq 7. The prime-power variable below is always separate from the base parameter. Finite seed calculations are printed, but nonvanishing at all sufficiently high powers follows from the residue-block identities proved here, not from extrapolating a finite table.

Lemma 11.2 (negative-base eventual nonvanishing).

For each r∈{2,3,4,5,6,7}r\in\{2,3,4,5,6,7\} and every fixed rational number ξ\xi, there is k0=k0⁢(r,ξ)k_{0}=k_{0}(r,\xi) such that

G4⁢prk,−r(V)⁢(ξ)≠0(k≥k0).G^{(V)}_{4p_{r}^{k},-r}(\xi)\neq 0\qquad(k\geq k_{0}).
Proof.

Use the convention vpr⁢(0)=+∞v_{p_{r}}(0)=+\infty. For all sufficiently large kk, vpr⁢(Q2⁢ξ)=2⁢k+vpr⁢(ξ)>0v_{p_{r}}(Q^{2}\xi)=2k+v_{p_{r}}(\xi)>0 (and this is immediate when ξ=0\xi=0). Since Pr,k∈ℤ(pr)⁢[X]P_{r,k}\in\mathbb{Z}_{(p_{r})}[X], its value at X=Q2⁢ξX=Q^{2}\xi is congruent modulo prp_{r} to its constant coefficient. By (11.10), that coefficient is a unit. Thus Pr,k⁢(Q2⁢ξ)≠0P_{r,k}(Q^{2}\xi)\neq 0, and the nonzero scaling in (11.8) yields the claim. ∎

11.5. Use in the determinant criterion

For a fixed rational target ξ\xi, the preceding lemmas give nonvanishing at every sufficiently high index of the selected prime-power sequence, not merely at one computed level. Once k≥k0k\geq k_{0}, the determinants at indices kk and k+1k+1 are both nonzero. This assertion concerns the selected prime-power subsequence only; no nonvanishing assertion is made for every intervening integer degree mm.

For each fixed integer base, the irrationality criterion of Section 3 must now be applied to one family at a time: P0 with its base-dependent prime, or V with the corresponding prp_{r}. The integerizer, analytic estimate, and nonzero determinant must all belong to that same source. The prime-power sequences proved here supply exactly the nonzero term required by the criterion; they do not by themselves imply a common analytic or arithmetic rate across the two families.

12. Hermite–Padé tails

This section proves the two tails from the displayed construction, without using an irrationality theorem as input. The base is fixed throughout each limit; constants in contour and remainder estimates may depend on that base.

13. Assembly of the proof

The positive construction supplies the criterion for 2≤n≤112\leq n\leq 11, the signed construction supplies it for −7≤n≤−2-7\leq n\leq-2, and the Hermite–Padé construction supplies it for n≥12n\geq 12 and n≤−8n\leq-8. Together with the two classical evaluations at n=±1n=\pm 1, these ranges prove Theorem 2.1.

Appendix A Positive endpoint data

The tables use ordinary decimal integers. Divide each mass list by the displayed denominator; the contour list gives the first half of the conjugate-symmetric Fejér weights, with zero filling at the remaining nodes.

Appendix B Exact signed reference data

Every entry below is an ordinary signed base-ten integer. For real chains, divide each length integer by 10810^{8} and each mass increment by 10810^{8}. A single listed correction (j,r)(j,r) adds r/(5⋅1013)r/(5\cdot 10^{13}) to length jj; j=0j=0 means no correction. Start each chain at its printed endpoint (units 1/(5⋅1013)1/(5\cdot 10^{13})), then accumulate lengths from left to right. Start each mass at zero and accumulate Δ⁢mi\Delta m_{i}. For Poisson rows divide all increments by 10810^{8}, accumulate coordinates and masses from zero, then append the reversed conjugates of all but the final (real) prefix row. Entries are read left to right and then top to bottom. These conventions, together with the displayed masses and supports, determine every reference measure uniquely.

Appendix C Exact certificate algorithm

All numerical bounds in this appendix are computer-assisted. The code and logs supplied as ancillary files use outward-rounded directed interval arithmetic; the rules below specify the calculation independently of those files. All inputs are the printed tables. Terminating decimals and fractions are parsed as exact rationals; a missing or duplicate field, invalid mass, failed strict inequality, or unresolved cell is fatal. No unprinted numerical data are part of the argument.

For a fixed reference 𝝂\boldsymbol{\nu}, let FiνF_{i}^{\nu} be the component potentials representing L⁢(𝝁)+2⁢B⁢(𝝂,𝝁)L(\boldsymbol{\mu})+2B(\boldsymbol{\nu},\boldsymbol{\mu}), and assume μi\mu_{i} and νi\nu_{i} have the same prescribed mass in each component. With 𝝈=𝝁−𝝂\boldsymbol{\sigma}=\boldsymbol{\mu}-\boldsymbol{\nu}, polarization gives the exact identity

ℰ⁢(𝝁)=C−Q⁢(𝝂)+∑i∫Fiν⁢𝑑μi+Q⁢(𝝈).\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{\mu})=C-Q(\boldsymbol{\nu})+\sum_{i}\int F_{i}^{\nu}\,% d\mu_{i}+Q(\boldsymbol{\sigma}).

Thus a nonnegative (respectively nonpositive) zero-mass remainder gives the lower (respectively upper) dual bound. The P0 and V proofs below differ only in the sign proof for this remainder and in their explicit transfer constants.

V reference tables.

The V data in Section B are printed as signed decimal integers in ordinary tables. In each real chain, the header gives the initial endpoint in units of 1/(5⋅1013)1/(5\cdot 10^{13}); each displayed length is in units of 10−810^{-8}, except for the single residual recorded by (j,r)(j,r) in the header, which adds r/(5⋅1013)r/(5\cdot 10^{13}) to length jj (the pair (0,0)(0,0) means no correction). Mass increments are in units of 10−810^{-8}. Starting from zero mass, accumulate each pair left to right and top to bottom. In each Poisson prefix, all three columns are successive increments of the real coordinate, imaginary coordinate, and mass, in units of 10−810^{-8}. The table header gives the prefix and full row counts; these must agree with Table 10.1. Complete the Poisson list by adjoining the reversed conjugates of all prefix rows except its final real row. The verification checks every count, increment, support, total mass, and conjugate pair. Real rows are uniform. A Poisson row is harmonic measure on |z|=r=3/5|z|=r=3/5, with density w⁢(r2−|c|2)/(2⁢π⁢|r⁢ei⁢θ−c|2)w(r^{2}-|c|^{2})/(2\pi|re^{i\theta}-c|^{2}) and potential w⁢log⁡|r2−z⁢c¯|−w⁢log⁡rw\log|r^{2}-z\bar{c}|-w\log r inside, w⁢log⁡|z−c|w\log|z-c| outside, and their common boundary value. It requires the exact strict test |c|2<r2|c|^{2}<r^{2}.
